articles.title: “Real Madrid Wins Trophies With Mourinho” Mourinho Claims Before El Clásico
articles.summary: Ahead of his first Clásico since returning to Real Madrid, José Mourinho stated that previous results do not matter as he discussed the game.
articles.body:
José Mourinho's first Clásico since returning to Real Madrid comes at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday night, and his opening message on the eve of it was that nothing his team has done so far counts.

"When we're on a roll, we play well, we score goals… but the Clásico isn't about what you've done before; it doesn't matter. It really is different," Mourinho said in his pre-match press conference on Saturday.

Kiyan Sobhani, host of the Managing Madrid podcast, has been a regular at Mourinho's press conferences this season and was in the room again on Saturday morning. "He was very stoic and didn't want to give anything away," Sobhani told me and it was clear, as on team selection, he gave away nothing at all. "I'm not going to answer that… let's ask another question instead," Mourinho said. "About plans, who's going to play, the line-up, I'm not going to answer." When the journalist reworded his question, Mourinho laughed, "you're clever, but I'm not stupid!". On almost everything else, the Mourinho of 2010 to 2013 was easy to find.

Earlier this week, Barcelona midfielder Fermín López said Madrid's complaints about referees were "getting tiresome" and that his team was focused on its own game. Mourinho needed one line to answer. "What can I say? We get fed up with other things, and yet they keep happening…"

He went further when asked about reports that referee Juan Martínez Munuera had paid for coaching from José María Enríquez Negreira, the former vice-president of the refereeing committee at the centre of the case against Barcelona. "That comes as a bit of a surprise to me," Mourinho said. "The referee's name never bothers me. I start from the premise that the referee is good; what bothers me is that the rules are being broken and, according to internal sources, this still isn't known. Three weeks ago one name came up, now another, but nobody internally has told me, 'the referee is official'."

Munuera's appointment was confirmed hours after the press conference. The Spanish football federation (RFEF) insisted that it would not name the Clásico referee until Saturday, 24 hours before kickoff, as is standard. That was despite reports in recent weeks that Alejandro Hernández Hernández, Spain's only referee at the 2026 World Cup, had already been appointed.

The numbers explain why Mourinho wanted to separate Sunday from everything before it, and everything to follow. Barcelona won their first 11 games of the season in all competitions before Paris Saint-Germain beat them 4-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday. Real Madrid's 4-1 win over Sevilla last Sunday, with two goals from Kylian Mbappé, cut Barcelona's lead at the top of LaLiga to six points, but a home win on Sunday would put Barcelona nine points clear.

Despite defeats already this season to Real Betis and Atlético Madrid, Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1 at the Bernabéu on Wednesday for a third win from three in the Champions League, after victories over Inter and Roma.

Mourinho dismissed the idea that the Paris result would rattle Barcelona, saying, "I don't think losing one match will change his state of mind or his confidence. Nor would it have changed me if we'd lost 4-1 to Leipzig."

He also pushed back on the comparison between the two squads. "We're seen as a finished product, and that's very difficult in football, but we're not at an advanced stage of that process; we've been working for three months, with a pre-season where players were arriving in pairs each week, then the break," he said. "Comparing a team at this stage with one that's been together for several years doesn't seem fair to me."

Questions about Barcelona coach Hansi Flick got shorter answers. "I don't understand the questions about our opponents. He's a great coach; he's doing a brilliant job. What do you want me to say?"

"Real Madrid win trophies with Mourinho"

The sharpest line came when he was asked whether Sunday was a test of whether this Real Madrid team could win titles. "No," he said. "Real Madrid win trophies with Mourinho."

His Clásico record from his first spell is less emphatic than that answer. Between 2010-11 and 2012-13, Mourinho's Madrid met Barcelona 17 times across LaLiga, the Copa del Rey, the Champions League and the Supercopa. They won five, drew six and lost six.

The first of those games is the one Barcelona fans still bring up, when Mourinho arrived at Camp Nou in November 2010 having made the best start of any Real Madrid coach in history, UEFA noted, and was unbeaten in his first 19 games. Pep Guardiola's Barcelona won 5-0 and Mourinho called it the heaviest defeat of his career. It was also his first return to the stadium where he had worked as Bobby Robson's translator in the 1990s.

The spring of 2011 brought four Clásicos in 18 days. Before the league meeting, Mourinho skipped the pre-match press conference and sent assistant Aitor Karanka in his place, prompting a walkout by some journalists. He did the same before the December 2011 Clásico, although this Saturday, he faced the room himself.

That April run produced his first win over Guardiola, 1-0 after extra time in the Copa del Rey final in Valencia, settled by a Cristiano Ronaldo header. A week later came the Champions League semi-final first leg at the Bernabéu. Madrid lost 2-0, Mourinho was sent to the stands. The low point arrived at the end of the Supercopa at Camp Nou in August 2011, when Mourinho poked Barcelona assistant Tito Vilanova in the eye during a touchline brawl. By January 2012, after a 2-2 Copa draw in Barcelona, he was claiming it was impossible to win there.

Three months later he did. Madrid won 2-1 at Camp Nou in April 2012, with Ronaldo scoring the winner. The result ended Barcelona's run of 55 home games unbeaten and effectively secured Madrid's first league title in four years. Mourinho finished his first spell unbeaten in his last five Clásicos, including a 3-1 Copa semi-final win at Camp Nou in February 2013.

That is the record he leaned on years later, when asked about his poor numbers against Guardiola. "I won the match for the title in Barcelona with Real Madrid," he told reporters. Saturday's answer about trophies came from the same place.

Mourinho played down any special significance in the venue. "It's just like playing at a different stadium. We're talking about a very strong side. But it's no big deal." He was happier talking about the fixture itself. "There are other important derbies in the world, but this is the one and only Clásico, the world comes to a standstill," he said.

On Sunday, the world will stop to take in one of soccer's greatest rivalries as Barcelona host Real Madrid at Spotify Camp Nou at 9pm local time (3pm ET) on Sunday, October 25.

articles.title: Man Utd urging patience with summer signing who ‘struggled’ in Como – Will he prove doubters wrong?
articles.summary: Manchester United are placing high hopes on Tynan Thompson, despite his early struggles at Carrington.The Premier League giants had an excessively quiet summ...
articles.body:
Manchester United are placing high hopes on Tynan Thompson, despite his early struggles at Carrington.

The Premier League giants had an excessively quiet summer transfer campaign. They almost exclusively focused on the midfield revamp, signing Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, and Carlos Baleba.

The only other first-team arrival was backup goalkeeper Karl Darlow. Nevertheless, INEOS made a few interesting moves in the youth section, and chief among them was Thompson .

Man Utd back Tynan Thompson to prove naysayers wrong

The 18-year-old is considered among the most exciting teenagers in the country after his exploits with Tottenham's U21 side last season.

Unlike other youngsters who were poached for free, Man Utd were happy to spend £8 million to secure Thompson's services.

The left winger was initially tipped to play a hybrid role between United's U21 side and Michael Carrick's first team, offering additional depth behind Matheus Cunha, Marcus Rashford, and Patrick Dorgu.

However, the early Carabao Cup elimination will hamper his chances of earning minutes. The London native has yet to make his senior debut, with no signs on the horizon.

On Wednesday, Thompson started for Man Utd's U19 team, which took on Como U19 in the UEFA Youth League.

While the young Reds didn't suffer a heavy defeat like the seniors later in the day, they still returned home empty-handed after losing 1-2 to their Italian hosts. Jack Fletcher's second-half goal wasn't enough to spark a comeback.

According to The Sun journalists Katherine Walsh and Samuel Luckhurst, Thompson 'struggled' in his outing against Como. The winger's performances are beginning to draw criticism from fans and observers.

Nevertheless, Man Utd still believe in the teenager's talent, tipping him to overcome his early difficulties and become an added asset to the first team at some point.

All judgement on Thompson should be postponed

Unfortunately for Thompson, he finds himself at a club engulfed by a toxic atmosphere. Even the youth sector has had its fair share of the drama, with JJ Gabriel refusing to play and trying to force his way out of the club.

If the most talented players in the senior squad haven't been able to find their footing since the start of the season, one can hardly blame a teenager for playing below his level, especially while he's still adjusting to his new surroundings.

Moreover, the metrics above prove he hasn't been as lacklustre as some are trying to paint him, as he's been able to provide his teammates with three assists.

Therefore, passing a judgment on Thompson would be incredibly immature at this stage.

articles.title: Bordalás: “Con Ángel Torres está todo hablado, nuestra relación será eterna”
articles.standfirst: El entrenador azulón analizó en sala de prensa la polémica que enovlió el choque frente al Lugano
articles.summary: El entrenador azulón analizó en sala de prensa la polémica que enovlió el choque frente al Lugano
articles.body: El entrenador del Getafe, José Bordalás, comparecía en sala de prensa en la previa del duelo frente al Athletic. El alicantino habló sobre la polémica que envolvió el postpartido frente al Lugano, sus palabras y las del presidente Ángel Torres, y señaló que ya está “todo olvidado” y que el cariño hacia el mandatario azulón “será eterno”. Palabras post Conference: “El problema o la preocupación de las declaraciones no son las declaraciones en sí del pasado jueves. El problema es que nos metieron cinco goles y a mí, como entrenador, es lo que me duele”. Declaraciones frente al Lugano: “Lo importante no son las declaraciones, ni las mías ni las de él. Fue lo que ocurrió. Nos duele a todos. He hablado con él, él sabe por qué hice estas declaraciones, que en ningún momento iban dirigidas a él. Está todo más que hablado. Sabe el cariño que le tengo, va a ser eterno ese cariño tanto a él, el Getafe...”. Conversación con Ángel Torres: “Hemos hablado, hemos analizado, ellos están dolidos como estamos todos porque fue una derrota muy dolorosa e inesperada. Estamos centrados en el partido de mañana en San Mamés contra el Athletic. El foco está en él. No ha habido tiempo para casi nada y esa es nuestra responsabilidad, intentar mejorar y que lo del pasado jueves no vuelva a ocurrir”. Pensando lo que dijo el jueves: “El presidente sabe por qué hice esas declaraciones, él cuando habló no sabía ni las había oído. Está todo más que aclarado, no voy a insistir en lo que pasó. Nuestra relación es fantástica, hemos estado hablando ayer, hoy ha estado en el entrenamiento. Nuestra relación va a ser eterna”. Necesidades: “Ya está todo aclarado, no tengo más que decir, el foco está en el partido frente al Athletic”. Enes Ünal: “Nos asustamos todos, la entrada fue muy fea y el gesto de su tobillo fue muy llamativo, pensábamos que podía haber lesión. Ha estado con dolor, pero ha entrenado con normalidad. Muy mala tiene que estar para no estar disponible. Va a estar seguro”. Athletic: “Hemos tenido muy poco tiempo, sabéis que no soy de excusas. Los lamentos no sirven de nada, hay que cambiar el chip y centrarnos en el partido. No hemos tenido mucho tiempo, pero el equipo está con ganas, con esa rabia, venimos de un resultado adverso, doloroso. Están los jugadores bien, con actitud, buena mentalidad y la confianza es máxima”. Cómo está: “Estoy fenomenal, no estéis tan preocupados. El ambiente es sanísimo. Entiendo vuestra pregunta, pero estamos de maravilla. Muchas gracias, agradezco esa preocupación, pero no estamos nada preocupados”. Zaid Romero, Mangala: “Esperábamos que estuvieran para este partido, pero al final no van a estar, está en la recta final de su recuperación e incorporación para poder trabajar con normalidad. Con tan poco tiempo era un riesgo muy alto, hemos preferido esperar unos días, ya están bastante bien, siempre es buena noticia recuperar jugadores”. Rotaciones: “Vamos a intentar sacar el once más competitivo, teniendo en cuenta muchas variantes, sobre todo minutos, eso es lo que hemos intentado estas últimas semanas. Vamos a jugar partidos muy seguidos. El de mañana tiene mucha exigencia, intentaremos sacar a los jugadores que más frescura tengan”. Tres competiciones: “No nos vamos a olvidar absolutamente de nada, tenemos que pensar en nuestra afición, que está ilusionada en todas las competiciones. Somos profesionales. Cuando llega LaLiga tenemos que poner nuestra energía y atención. Cuando llegue Copa, lo mismo, y cuando tengamos que jugar Conference, igual, así sucesivamente. Soy muy exigente, es una obligación como profesional y los jugadores son conscientes de que tenemos una responsabilidad. Tenemos que crecer y mejorar paulatinamente”.

articles.title: Infantino says he is backed by 'vast majority'
articles.summary: Fifa president Gianni Infantino laughs off questions about whether he considered resigning over the World Cup sell-off debacle.
articles.body:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino insists he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football, as he laughed off questions about whether he had considered resigning over the World Cup sell-off debacle.

In a rare interview, he struck a defiant tone to BBC Sport about his own position in the wake of the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and said it was not always easy to bring different points of view "under one roof".

"There is nothing bad in disagreeing," he said. "We see it every day in so many countries in the world. It's OK to disagree. It's OK to have different points of view, but then we need to be able to move on."

Two months ago, Infantino was facing mounting calls to stand down as president of the organisation he has led since 2016.

The heads of European football's governing body Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf, which runs the game in North and Central America, signed a letter accusing the Fifa president of breaking trust "through deception".

Last week Uefa demanded that Fifa release all key documents relating to FFE by 2 November, with Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis saying that the organisation had failed to address "a number of fundamental questions".

Under FFE, which Infantino scrapped within days, a portion of the commercial rights of football's world governing body would have been sold to a private investment firm.

Since the delivery of the letter, Infantino has been travelling the world, appearing in Morocco, the Dominican Republic, Cape Verde, and Japan, managing to shore up support to the point where his re-election as president for a fourth term next year now looks inevitable.

He has also proposed to increase the amount of money handed out for football development across the world by $3.4bn (£2.6bn).

Fifa has done some things 'maybe less good'

During the interview he reflected on having been "fully endorsed" by the Asian Football Confederation - following a U-turn by its president Sheikh Salman - and having the backing of "all African countries".

But only last week, he apologised to the Fifa Council over the "communication and consultation" regarding FFE.

He was told by Council members in that meeting that he was not "fit to be Fifa president" if he did not give them the documents they have asked for, including the rationale for FFE.

Yet, when pressed on when he would be providing the requested papers, he did not give a clear answer, saying they had to follow a "legal process" and that they were "working on it".

"We'll answer of course all the questions that are asked as far as the process allows, as far as we can," he said.

Speaking from the first Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, he said he and the Fifa administration were doing "as best we can" but admitted they have done "some things which are maybe less good".

He also said that they need to have dialogue "more often" with Uefa, in an effort to repair their strained relationship.

Asked by the BBC if he was fit to be Fifa president, and whether he had considered standing down, he laughed, before saying: "Well you know I was elected by 211 member associations from all over the world.

"I think what is important is that in an organisation like Fifa, there can be different views, different points of view.

"But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need, to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority.

"I'm just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all [Confederation of] African [Football] countries have endorsed me. I'm speaking to all associations everywhere in the world."

He continued: "There are different points of view it's not always easy to bring them all under one roof but we need to respect and I do respect all opinions all views and then it will be up to the Fifa member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want Fifa to be run."

The deadline for candidates to confirm they are standing against Infantino for the election in March is 18 November - although none have yet filed and he could stand unopposed.

Infantino arrived in Baku on Friday for the Fifa Under-15 World Cup and Festival, which is being held in Azerbaijan and features teams from 189 member associations.

England, Spain, France, Argentina and Brazil are all taking part. Russia have also sent a team, marking the country's first appearance in a Fifa-sanctioned tournament since the world governing body, and Uefa, suspended Russian teams from international competitions in February 2022 following the invasion of Ukraine.

This tournament is only for boys, with next year's tournament being girls only, and then from 2028 Fifa's plan is to have boys and girls competing in the tournament annually.

Matches are played in an 8v8 format, on smaller pitches and with 20-minute halves.

"It's just beautiful to bring the world together at such a young age to create something like this," Infantino said.

"When some of these boys participate in a World Cup 10 years, 20 years from now, they will all remember that their first World Cup was here."
authors: Laura Scott - Sports News Correspondent in Baku

articles.title: Jose Mourinho hits back at 'unfair' comparisons between Real Madrid and Barcelona ahead of El Clasico
articles.summary: Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has dismissed suggestions that his side should already be at the same level as Barcelona, labelling such comparisons as...
articles.body:
Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has dismissed suggestions that his side should already be at the same level as Barcelona, labelling such comparisons as "unfair" ahead of Sunday's showdown. The Portuguese tactician faces a tough test at Camp Nou with his team trailing the league leaders by six points in the La Liga standings.

Mourinho has played down the hype surrounding the latest edition of El Clasico, insisting that his Madrid side remains a work in progress compared to the established machine at Barcelona. Despite a recent uptick in form, including four consecutive victories and a convincing 4-1 Champions League win over RB Leipzig , the former Chelsea boss believes people are overlooking the difference in stability between the two Spanish giants.

"I think the people that thought a week ago Barca would thrash us will keep thinking the same thing. I don't think just for the Paris game, or Madrid's (4-1 win against) Leipzig, they will change their way of thinking," Mourinho stated, as quoted by RTL .

The Madrid manager was keen to highlight that while Hansi Flick has had significant time to implement his philosophy at Barcelona since arriving earlier in 2024, the situation at the Santiago Bernabeu is vastly different. Mourinho arrived this summer following a two-season drought of major silverware for Los Blancos, and he is adamant that his squad is still in its infancy under his stewardship.

The coach noted that his time with the full squad has been severely limited due to post-World Cup breaks and recent international windows, leaving little room for tactical cohesion on the training pitch. "People look at us like a finished product, but finished products in football are difficult because they are never finished... but they look at us like we're in an advanced phase of the process," Mourinho continued.

"We've been working for three months, out of that you can take pre-season when the players were arriving (back from the World Cup), and the recent international break, then we've been together a month-and-a-half, two months... This is the start of a product, we're in an initial phase where the coach is learning, analysing, bit by bit defining paths, the players are learning about the coach... comparing a team in this state (to more established sides), I think is unfair."

Despite the six-point gap in the table and Barca's domestic dominance, Mourinho is refusing to let previous results dictate the mood heading into the weekend. While Barcelona recently suffered a rare setback against PSG , Madrid enter the contest with momentum, but the coach insists that history and recent form count for very little once the whistle blows in Catalonia.

"We've been in a good dynamic, winning games, playing well, scoring goals, but in the Clasico it doesn't matter what you did before, it has no influence. The Clasico is unique, normally the football world stops to watch it. Hopefully it's a great game. And we win," the coach remarked.

A major talking point ahead of the fixture is the form of Lamine Yamal, with the 19-year-old Spaniard widely tipped to be a frontrunner for the Ballon d'Or. However, Mourinho made it clear that while he acknowledges the teenager's immense talent, he will not be tearing up his tactical blueprint specifically to nullify the Barcelona winger's influence on the right flank.

"He's a great player and great players you respect," Mourinho added when questioned about his defensive strategy. "One thing is respecting, another thing is to change plans, structures, forgetting your own essence. That we will not do, neither for him or any other player of great quality we face."

articles.title: 'I hit a breaking point' - Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo opens up on mental health struggle and decision to quit football temporarily before Liverpool move
articles.summary: Liverpool defender Ronald Araujo has delivered a powerful and honest account of his battle with depression, revealing he reached a "breaking point" that forc...
articles.body:
Liverpool defender Ronald Araujo has delivered a powerful and honest account of his battle with depression, revealing he reached a "breaking point" that forced him to step away from the game. The Uruguayan international, currently on loan at Anfield from Barcelona, admitted that the pressures of professional football and personal issues became overwhelming during his time in Spain.

Last November, the 27-year-old found himself spiralling into depression while playing for Barcelona. His underlying struggles culminated following a dismissal against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge . In the aftermath of that match, his family became the target of horrific death threats, prompting the defender to finally confront his deteriorating mental health.

Recognising the severity of his situation, Araujo temporarily stepped away from the sport . During his month-long sabbatical away from the Catalan giants, he leaned heavily on his Christian faith and began working with psychological professionals to address complex issues extending far beyond the pitch.

Speaking to Paul Joyce of The Times , Araujo detailed the heavy emotional toll he endured. The 27-year-old centre-back explained that his temporary retirement was entirely necessary to rediscover his passion for the sport.

"It was a very difficult time," Araujo admitted. "I felt that what I needed to do was take a step back. I hadn't felt right for a long time, and I wasn't enjoying the thing I love most, which is football."

The Uruguayan highlighted the importance of abandoning the facade of invulnerability, noting that the Stamford Bridge incident was merely the tipping point for long-standing personal issues. "I realised I had to put my hand up, ask for help and talk not just to the people closest to me, but to professionals as well," he added. "Sometimes you bottle things up and try to be the strong man, but in life you have to talk about things and open up about what you're going through."

He further explained his abrupt departure from the Barcelona squad last autumn: "I made the decision after being sent off at Stamford Bridge because that was the breaking point. I just couldn't carry on any longer, but it wasn't down to any one particular incident. A lot of things had been building up, particularly in my personal life, and I didn't know how to deal with them.

"Sometimes people generalise and assume that because footballers earn a lot of money, we can't suffer or struggle. But we go through the same things as anyone else. There's more to life than football."

Sparking a wider conversation across football

Araujo's transparency has deeply resonated across the footballing landscape. Following his initial time away, Barcelona's coaching staff and his teammates offered unwavering support . Crucially, his public vulnerability encouraged peers worldwide to privately share their own hidden battles with him.

"I had a lot of players from different leagues get in touch with me. I see it when I speak to teammates, not just at Liverpool but with the national team too," Araujo revealed. "There are a lot of players going through difficult times, but they're afraid to talk about it publicly. It's important to open up because that's when you start to feel better."

Now thriving during his loan spell on Merseyside, the defender credits that critical hiatus for saving both his career and his wellbeing. "Taking that break was the best decision I've ever made," he declared. "Today, I feel good, I'm happy and I'm enjoying football again, and that shows on the pitch. Now I can show what I'm really capable of again."

With his mental health now in a much stronger place, Araujo will look to maintain his impressive form as Liverpool prepare to host high-flying Brighton in the Premier League. Meanwhile, his parent club faces a massive test on Sunday night, with Barcelona preparing to take on arch-rivals Real Madrid in a highly anticipated Clasico showdown.

articles.title: Real Madrid consider activating €80 million buyback clause for Nico Paz in 2027 – report
articles.summary: Real Madrid are reportedly considering bringing Nico Paz back to the club in 2027 by activating an €80 million buy-back clause, according to Spanish journali...
articles.body:
Real Madrid are reportedly considering bringing Nico Paz back to the club in 2027 by activating an €80 million buy-back clause, according to Spanish journalist Ramon Alvarez .

The Argentine attacking midfielder has made significant progress at Como under Cesc Fabregas, strengthening the case for a potential return to the Santiago Bernabeu.

Real Madrid eye Nico Paz return from Como

Real Madrid have begun looking ahead to the 2027/28 campaign, assessing potential reinforcements, particularly in defence and midfield.

The Merengues are also monitoring former academy players who have developed impressively after leaving Madrid.

And Nico Paz is one of the most prominent examples. The Argentine has continued to enhance his reputation at Como, where he has developed under former Barcelona midfielder Fabregas.

Excelling at Como. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

His performances have reportedly kept Real Madrid interested in bringing him back, with Ramon Alvarez claiming that the club want to exercise the €80 million buyback option for the Argentine playmaker.

The reported fee would represent a substantial investment in a player the Spanish giants already know from their academy system.

Real Madrid re-signed Nico Paz this past summer only to sell him back to Como as the youngster sought to continue his development at Como rather than returning to the Santiago Bernabeu.

The decision has proved to be the right one as the 22-year-old Argentine playmaker has excelled for Como, managing four goals and five assists in ten games.

Will Nico Paz return to Real Madrid in 2027? (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

As part of the new agreement, the Spanish capital club retained another buyback option worth €80 million for 2027.

Nico Paz faces a potential midfield selection dilemma at Real Madrid

Paz's progress at Como gives Real Madrid a compelling reason to consider bringing him back, but finding him a regular role could prove complicated.

Real Madrid already have considerable competition in attacking midfield, with Jude Bellingham a leading option in the position. Arda Guler also offers an alternative, creating a potential selection challenge if Paz returns.

The club would therefore need to weigh the Argentine's growing potential against the demands of building a balanced squad. After all, substantial investment would naturally bring expectations around his playing time and role within the team.
